question.problem:
The solution to the inequality $-10x-13<17$ is$\,x$
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, adding $13$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-10x-13 & <17 \\ -10x-13+13 & <17+13 \\ -10x+0 & <30 \\ -10x & <30\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $-10.$ 

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-10x\,\, & <\,\,30 \\ \frac{-10x}{-10}\, & >\,\,\frac{30}{-10} \\ \frac{\cancel{-10}x}{\cancel{-10}}\, & >\,\,-3 \\ x\,\, & >\,-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x>-3.$
